text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- More than 700 employees of central bank, Bank Negara will be retrenched and six of its 12 branches closed under a rationalisation plan to improve operations, said Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim
-- A one billion ringgit naval base will be built about 25 km from the Sabah state capital of Kota Kinabalu, said Defence Minister Syead Hamid Albar.
-- KKB Engineering Bhd has confirmed it was negotiating for contracts related to the Bakun dam project in sarawak state, said group managing director Kho Kak Beng.

-- Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Abul Hassan Chowdhury and High Commissioner Mustafa Kamaluddin apologised for social problems created by its nationals in Malaysia and promised to revamp recruitment network. Recent newspaper reports highlighted fights and tensions between groups of Bangladeshi workers and Malaysian villagers.

-- The Information Ministry will issue new broadcasting guidelines soon for TV and radio stations to ensure all programes aired contain positive moral and cultural values, said Information Minister Mohamed Rahmat.
